newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh teachers strike, demand unpaid salaries.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh teachers strike, demand unpaid salaries.

text.p: Around 1,500 teachers in Kazakhstan's eastern Semipalatinsk region went on strike on Thursday demanding months of unpaid backpay, a trade union official said.
"Teachers in the region have only one demand -- they need their honestly-earned salaries," a spokeswoman for the Trade Union of People's Education told Reuters by phone in the Kazakh capital Almaty.

She said the school teachers stopped working on Thursday morning in 20 secondary schools in the regional capital Semipalatinsk. She added teachers in the Kokshetau, Pavlodar and Almaty regions were also considering strike action.
Authorities in Semipalatinsk owe the region's teachers a total of 400 million tenge ($5.27 million) in salary arrears. Many of them have not been paid since October.
Kazakh President Nursultan Nazarbayev has said the former Soviet republic's spiralling backlog of unpaid wages -- an estimated 60 billion tenge ($800 million) -- threatened social stability.
He has threatened to sack government and regional officials who fail to improve the situation by April 1.
Earlier this week, dozens of workers at a power plant in the town of Karaganda in central Kazakhstan went on hunger strike over unpaid wages.
